title: Adaptive intake lanes for model variants, automated pin suggestions, and enterprise quarantine path
creator: Aisha Navarro
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers increasingly request explicit version pinning, rapid model additions, and predictable deprecation paths. Current intake is manual and binary (fast-track vs normal), which causes delays for models that are low-risk but important for customer workflows. There is also limited automation to suggest pin durations or quarantine a model for extra review when eval signals are unstable.

Proposal: Create an adaptive intake system with three lanes: (1) Fast Onboard (low-risk, auto-accept), (2) Quarantine Review (enterprise-impacting, needs gated eval), and (3) Shadow Trial (for gradual adoption with monitoring). Build an automated "pin suggestion" engine that computes a recommended pin duration and risk score using: eval pass/fail stability, latency/cost delta vs catalog baseline, and customer SLA tier. Provide UI affordances in the Console to accept suggested pins, override, or request manual review. Wire the flow to eval gates (auto-run a standardized eval set on staging), and trigger a deprecation workflow when models drift beyond thresholds.

Scope: PM + Eng + DX. Deliverables: intake rules engine, pin-suggestion service (stateless scoring lambda), Console intake UI changes (accept/override), eval-runner integration for quarantine lane, and rollout plan for enterprise customers to opt into automated suggestions. Not in scope: model training, model-level security features (handled separately by Security team).
acceptance_criteria: Intake UI exposes three lanes and lets PM/SE pick or accept suggested lane
Pin suggestion service returns a numeric pin recommendation and risk rationale for 90% of incoming model requests in test data
Quarantine lane triggers an automated eval run and posts results to the intake ticket within 30 minutes
Shadow Trial lane can route 5% of traffic to new model variant and collect quality/latency metrics for 7 days
Console shows a clear audit trail for pin decisions and links to eval results (for compliance)
updates: 2026-02-20: Initial scoping session with Eng (Liam Chen), Research (Dr. Priya Desai) and Solutions (Marcus Hale). Consensus to prototype pin-suggestion heuristics before full rollout.
2026-02-26: Prototype spec added to Confluence; Eng estimated 5 points. Action: Eng to spike an offline scoring script using historical catalog onboarding data.

2026-03-03: Spike complete. Early scoring model uses three signals (eval stability, latency delta, customer tier). Preliminary precision 78% for conservative pins. Feedback from Research: incorporate rollback cost estimator.
2026-03-08: Design review — Console intake modal mockups (Figma) reviewed; requested inline rationale copy for suggested pins and a compact view for fast accept. Design owner: Nia Alvarez.

2026-03-10: Product review meeting. Decision: move to Planned and start implementation in Cycle 2026-W10. Next steps: ENG to implement scoring endpoint (ENG-1842 dependency), PM to draft rollout communication and opt-in plan for enterprise customers.
